title: Getting In: gcloud compute ssh, IAP Tunnels, and the Serial Console
intro: 'gcloud compute ssh' manages SSH keys for you. For VMs with no external IP, Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) tunnels SSH through Google's edge, so nothing is exposed to the internet. When SSH is broken entirely, the serial port output shows what the VM is doing.

steps.fake_output:
Updating project ssh metadata...done.
Warning: Permanently added 'compute.482910381204' (ED25519) to the list of known hosts.
alice@web-1:~$
steps.explanation: gcloud generated a key, pushed it to the VM, and connected.
steps.why: Pushing keys into project metadata works, but with OS Login (enable-oslogin=TRUE) SSH access is controlled by IAM roles instead (roles/compute.osLogin), and removed automatically when someone leaves. OS Login is the enterprise default.

steps.prompt: worker-1 (europe-west1-b) has no external IP. SSH to it through IAP.
steps.fake_output:
External IP address was not found; defaulting to using IAP tunneling.
alice@worker-1:~$
steps.explanation: Connected through IAP with no public IP and no bastion host.
steps.why: IAP authorises each connection with IAM (roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor) and logs it. The VM's firewall only needs to allow SSH from IAP's range, 35.235.240.0/20, not from the internet. Forgetting that rule is gcp-incident-004.

steps.prompt: SSH to worker-1 fails for a colleague. Let gcloud diagnose the connection.
steps.fake_output:
---- Checking network connectivity ----
No firewall rule allows ingress from 35.235.240.0/20 on port 22 for this VM.
---- Checking user permissions ----
User is missing roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor.
---- Checking VM status ----
VM is RUNNING. Guest agent is healthy.
steps.explanation: Two problems: no firewall rule for IAP, and a missing IAM role.
steps.why: --troubleshoot checks the network path, IAM, the VM and the guest environment in one go, and names what's wrong. Use it before debugging SSH by hand.

steps.prompt: A third VM, cache-1 in europe-west1-b, won't answer at all. Read its serial port output.
expected_commands: gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output cache-1 --zone europe-west1-b
steps.fake_output:
[  OK  ] Started Google Compute Engine Guest Agent.
[    3.412] EXT4-fs error (device sda1): ext4_lookup:1601: inode #2: comm systemd: deleted inode referenced
[FAILED] Failed to start File System Check on /dev/sda1.
Give root password for maintenance (or press Control-D to continue):
steps.explanation: The root filesystem check failed, and the VM is waiting at a maintenance prompt.
steps.why: The serial console output works when the network and SSH don't, like 'aws ec2 get-console-output' and Azure boot diagnostics. The same failures show up on every cloud: fstab, filesystem errors, full disks, kernel panics.

steps.prompt: Reach a private web UI on worker-1's port 8080 from your laptop, tunnelled through IAP to local port 8080.
steps.fake_output:
Testing if tunnel connection works.
Testing if tunnel connection works...done.
Listening on port [8080].
steps.explanation: http://localhost:8080 on your laptop now reaches worker-1:8080 privately.
steps.why: IAP tunnels work for any TCP port, not just SSH. It's the safe way to reach admin UIs (a queue dashboard, a database admin tool) without exposing them.
